questions.question: Give three reasons why Mapungubwe is called the first town in southern Africa.
questions.expected_answer: About five thousand people lived there close together. Many people did specialised work, such as pottery, metal working, ivory carving, bead making and cotton spinning. It was the centre of trade for a large area, sending gold and ivory to the coast and receiving beads and cloth, and it was the centre of power where the king lived.

questions.question: Describe the three social classes at Mapungubwe.
questions.expected_answer: At the top was the royal class, the king and royal family, who lived on the hilltop, controlled trade and were buried with gold. In the middle were important people or the elite, such as advisers, officials and lesser chiefs, who helped the king rule and lived near the hill. At the bottom were ordinary people, the largest group, farmers, herders, craft workers and hunters who lived in the valley.

questions.question: Explain why the golden rhino and other golden objects are seen as symbols of royal power.
questions.expected_answer: Gold was rare, beautiful and did not rust, so it showed great wealth. Only the most powerful people could get gold and pay skilled smiths to work it. The golden rhino, bowl and sceptre were buried only with members of the royal class, so they marked the difference between the king and ordinary people.
